source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: if it be on the actual horizon, or succedent to the horizon, it is also powerful—particularly if in the eastern quarter

calculation_dependencies: angular position relative to the horizon
normalized_rule: Classify a planet's influence as powerful when it is on the actual horizon or succedent to the horizon, especially in the eastern quarter.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific traditional influence classification, not a modern physics or house-rulership claim.
review_notes: Keep this horizon condition separate from the mid-heaven and below-horizon conditions in the same chapter.
transmission_notes: The condition is stated in the Ashmand/Proclus main text; no later house-rulership or accidental-dignity system is imported.
